references.text: Part of the same section on unintentional sins requiring a guilt offering, where someone fails to testify about something they have seen or heard.
Concerns vows and oaths made to the Lord, and the obligation to keep what one has promised with their lips.
Emphasizes the importance of keeping promises made with one's lips, and that a vow to the Lord must be fulfilled.
Warns against making hasty vows to God, stating it is better not to promise than to promise and fail to fulfill.
Describes the righteous person who keeps their oath even when it brings harm to themselves.
Jephthah's rash vow that he had to keep, an example of the consequences of thoughtless promises.
Saul's hasty oath that caused trouble for the people and his son Jonathan.
Jesus teaches about oaths, saying one should not swear at all, but let their yes be yes and their no be no.
James warns against swearing, neither by heaven nor by earth, but to let your yes be yes and your no be no.
